sections.heading: A boundary that does useful work
sections.body: A cell membrane is selectively permeable. Osmosis is water movement across a selectively permeable membrane. With equal initial pressure, water tends to move toward the side with more solute that cannot cross.
sections.visual: More water crosses toward the side with more trapped solute. Individual water molecules move both ways; the larger arrow shows net movement before pressure balances it.

sections.heading: Lower the barrier, keep the destination
sections.body: An enzyme supplies a pathway with a lower activation barrier, increasing reaction rate. Catalysis does not change overall free-energy difference or equilibrium.
sections.visual: The enzyme provides a route with a lower activation-energy barrier. Reactant and product energies stay the same.

sections.heading: Count alleles before predicting traits
sections.body: For an Aa × Aa cross, the four equally likely combinations are AA, Aa, aA and aa. With complete dominance, AA and Aa share the dominant phenotype, producing a 3:1 phenotype ratio.
sections.visual: Each cell combines one allele from each parent. The genotype ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. With complete dominance, three of the four outcomes have the dominant phenotype.
